Bhai,

Being fellow Malayalees, every one of our conversations started the same way - you'd say "bhai," I'd say it right back. But nothing that followed was ever small talk. Every conversation with you - on design, on product, on the business behind it all - I walked out having learned something.
You're one of the most knowledgeable people I've worked with, across a genuinely wide range of things, and that combination is rare.
What I've admired most is how candid you are. You speak your mind, always, and that kind of honesty is harder to find than people think.

As a design team, we've looked up to you as a strong proponent of customer obsession and good UX. You gave us more than direction - you gave us a reason to stand firmly on the user's side and advocate for them, always.

You've also been a role model for building a builder's attitude in the team - Thursday Club, the collaborative learning sessions, the fun-loving culture you brought into everything. And of course, the one-liners. The puns. I'm a genuine fan.

I loved hearing about the side projects too - the things you built just because you wanted to, some of them just for your kids. You've built a lot. Now go launch some of them ( :P ). The energy you brought to those conversations was infectious. Honestly, it's part of what pushed me back to the drawing board on a few of my own old ideas that I'd never found the motivation to finish.

Thank you, Narayan, for all the learning, and for being such a strong leader for PayZapp Studio. We'll miss you. Wherever you go next, keep building, keep breaking things, and keep being exactly who you are.
Take care Bhai.

And of course, I will really miss the way you used to crack jokes and make everyone laugh around you. You had a wonderful way of bringing lightness and fun to even the busiest days.
Your presence is truly powerful, and I feel really lucky to have had the opportunity to work with you so closely and manage things alongside you. It has been an experience I will always cherish.
Thank you for all the learning, support, trust, guidance, and wonderful memories. You will definitely be missed!
Wishing you nothing but the very best for this next chapter. Keep shining, keep inspiring, and keep being the amazing all-rounder that you are.

Dear Narayan,

It's hard to put into words what these 4 years and 10 months have meant from Plutus to Payzapp studio, but I'll try.  I've rarely met anyone with as much genuine passion for technology as you — the ideas and perspectives you bring to the table are consistently insightful and refreshingly out of the box. What makes you truly special is that you never kept that brilliance to yourself; you ensured the entire team grew alongside you, going out of your way to help the team excel and navigate every challenge together. You consistently put the team first, making sure we felt comfortable and supported.
You never hesitated to say yes when we wanted to do something for the team, and that trust meant a great deal to us. It has been an honor working with you and getting to know you so closely.

I'll always cherish our morning chats ☕ — they were like your quiet warm-up before the BEARN & EARN connects😉. I'd join in a few minutes early, and we'd end up having the sweetest, most spontaneous conversations. Thank you for always making time to listen.

I'll miss the countless war rooms, the Thursday Club, townhalls, A&B Felicitations, team engagements, staff connects — simply too many moments to count, and every time you'd ask us what unhealthy snacks we were going to order 😉
And of course, there's the offsite where your car broke down — still one of the funniest stories we have 🚗😂. Not to forget your go-to exercise, push-ups, which you never skipped, whether in the office or at offsites. 💪 This page truly isn't enough to hold all these memories.

And who could forget the memories from the Plutus Leadership meetings — your self-appointed role of collecting contributions from anyone who stepped in late, all in the name of ordering everyone's favorite Ferrero Rocher chocolates 😄

Your passion for football ⚽ and the way you encourage your son to be his best is inspiring to watch. Your love for coffee ☕and Indian sweets 🍬, cars 🚙, fitness (counting those calories like a true perfectionist 😄), and your Meta glasses — I'll miss those conversations and watching you use them on the floor. Your love for music 🎶 rounds it all out and of course, how can I forget the PJs there's simply so much to you, Narayan, much like the person you are. Your weekend getaways to the farmhouse 🌳 — I hope to visit someday; I've heard and seen so much about everything you've built there with your own hands. And of course, your legendary rollercoaster of a house project 🎢 — hoping it's finally complete, or still happily in progress!

Thank you as well for your warmth and care — every time I took sick leave, for myself or my family, you checked in to see how things were. That gesture meant more than you know, and it's something I'll always remember. 🙏
There was simply too much to capture in a video, so I wanted to put it in writing instead.
Thank you, sincerely, for everything. It has been a privilege working with and learning from you. Thank you for standing by us, always. This isn't goodbye — we'll stay in touch. 🤝
Wishing you continued success in whatever comes next — I have no doubt you'll shine, because for you, the sky was never the limit. ✨
Until next time, Narayan. 👋

With gratitude and best wishes,
Violet Fernandes

Hi Narayan, it's been really great working with you! Dear Narayan,
A big thank you for everything you've done for PayZapp and for the engineering culture you've helped build over the last four years.

Even though I had the opportunity to work with you as my manager for only a brief period, your impact has been truly lasting. You introduced concepts like Domain-Driven Design and Clean Architecture to PayZapp and, more importantly, changed the way engineers think about building products. The discipline of first documenting the use cases and defining the entity model gave us a strong foundation and played a huge role in helping us build a quality product.

You also brought a strong startup culture to PayZapp through initiatives like the Thursday Club. Under your guidance, we had many successful Thursday Clubs that brought engineers together to experiment, brainstorm, build, and think like product owners rather than simply focusing on their day-to-day tasks. I especially feel this had a great impact on the newer folks joining PayZapp, helping them develop a strong product mindset right from the beginning.

What I've always admired is your mindset of experimenting, challenging the status quo, and striving for a pixel-perfect experience. You encouraged everyone to think beyond routine execution and constantly look for ways to add that extra "wow" factor to what we build.
Thank you for guiding and inspiring us right from the inception of PayZapp. Your energy, passion, and presence on the floor will truly be missed.
Wishing you all the very best for your next chapter. I'm sure you'll continue to create the same impact wherever you go.
Thank you, Narayan, and all the very best for your future endeavours! 🙏
Hey Narayan, just wanted to say a very big thank you for all the trust you've placed in me over these years, and all the opportunities you've helped me with.

One thing I definitely want to call out — and I hope this never changes — is that you don't mind being the unpopular voice in the room when you truly believe in something. You stand up for what is right. I truly appreciate that about you, and of course your candour.

This isn't really a farewell message — but what I'll definitely miss is our candid conversations over lunch, where you'd tell me about all the new tech you'd explored, whatever you were building, your side projects, and so on.
I don't think this changes how often we talk — but I'll miss having you physically in the office. I'm very excited about what you're building next, and I'm sure I'll be watching closely.

blocks.value: Hi Narayan — I was thinking about which moments I recollect, and funnily, the only ones that come to mind are all somehow sports-related.

We were in an inception once, following the India–England Test. Siraj was bowling. We needed ten wickets. I think the two of us were the only ones actively following ball by ball — and before the final wicket fell, you made us stop the meeting so we could both see the last five minutes.
And of course all our football moments — playing with you, all those Sundays, the tournament where you injured your hand. Apart from work, that's what I remember most.

What I want to share personally is how much you're doing outside of work. That stands out as clear inspiration — seeing you do all of that so well inspired me to ask why I wasn't doing more. Over the past six to eight months I've got a 3D printer, built websites, an app for my wife and the baby that only the three of us use — and I just love being a builder again. A lot of the credit for that comes from watching what you're able to do at such a high level.
I'll keep bugging you with things I build for feedback. We'll definitely miss having you around. I'm sure you'll kill whatever you decide to do next — all the best, and stay in touch.
